I have a specialty Visa with Chase bank. A few months ago, I took advantage of a balance transfer offer that they gave me and transferred a $ XXXX balance to that card ( which previously had a {$0.00} balance ). A month later, I used that same card to take a vacation with my son. This particular specialty card provides XXXX XXXX discounts when used at the vacation destination that we were at. So it made sense for me to use that card in this instance as well. 

For the last couple of months, I have made payments of {$1000.00} or more each month expecting that those payments would be applied to the highest interest balance on the account ( what I charged on vacation ) as is required ( from my understanding ) by law rather than them being applied to the XXXX XXXX balance transfer balance. I noticed today however, that of the {$1300.00} I paid last month, {$890.00} of those payments were applied to the XXXX XXXX balance transfer and only {$400.00} was applied to the roughly {$6000.00} 19.49 % interest rate balance. 

I contacted Chase several times because the answers I was provided on a couple of the calls didn't add up to " math '' and what was on my statements. I finally spoke to an escalations person who informed me that " normally '' they would apply payments to the highest interest-bearing balance on the card but since I took advantage of a balance transfer, in the fine print of that offer, allowed them to only apply my monthly minimum payment to the higher interest balance and any overages I pay would go to the XXXX XXXX balance transfer. She also informed me that there was no way they had to allow the consumer to call or through their website to make any payments and designate which balance to apply that to. 

So basically, I will be unable to pay off the higher interest balance until I pay off the XXXX XXXX balance transfer. This allows them to continue to charge the 19.49 % interest on the other part of my balance. Which pretty much makes the balance transfer savings pointless. While I'm not sure if this is legal or not, if it is, it shouldn't be. Nowhere evident in the balance transfer process was I informed of this process or change to the standard payment application process on the card. There have been tons of laws requiring " truth in lending '' to consumers through credit card statements and loan applications so I can't imagine that this isn't borderline illegal. I am happy to provide any additional information needed.
